## 1. Guidance and results
- Q1 FY27 revenue was $19.3B (+30%) against consensus of about $19.13B. writeup.headline: Oracle rates Hold: strong AI-driven growth offset by heavy cash burn and a collapsed share price trend.
writeup.thesis: Oracle scores 50, a Hold with high confidence, because standout growth is cancelled out by weak trend, cash flow and valuation readings. Growth scores 86, with quarterly revenue up 29.61% year on year and accelerating by 8.98 points versus the trailing twelve months. Quality scores only 48: the 32.12% operating margin is solid, but free cash flow margin is -40.01% as AI data-center spending consumes cash, and share count dilution is 3.13%. The trend factor scores 1, with the stock 58.29% below its 52-week high and 18.83% below its 200-day average. Valuation scores 43 and news risk 56, as strong guidance and a $664B backlog are balanced by litigation and a data breach.
key_risks: Deeply negative free cash flow (-40.01% margin) from AI capex; the capex early-warning check is AMBER at 6/18.
Possible customer concentration: a low-reliability, unverified source links about half of the $664B backlog to AI labs, with OpenAI a large share.
Data-center delays, including flagged risk at Project Jupiter, could push out revenue.
Pending securities class action and an Oracle Health breach affecting nearly 20M individuals.
Severe price weakness: momentum of -53.99% and underperformance versus SPY by 33.08 points.
what_would_change: A drop of 6 points in the composite score (below 45) would move the rating to Sell, for example from further trend weakness or a worsening news-risk score.
Rising 15 points to 65 would require broad improvement, such as free cash flow turning positive to lift quality and valuation.
A recovery in the share price trend from its score of 1 would add meaningful points given its 15% weight.
Escalation of the AI capex warning beyond AMBER, or a guidance cut from the FY27 target of at least $90B revenue, would push the rating down.
